member.name: T:Xmip.Abi.Module.ModuleProbe
member.summary: Loads a module through the C ABI and reports what it says about itself.
member.remarks:
ADR-0012 leaves one thing open: "a conformance suite able to drive the seven rules in its section 11 from outside a module". This is the first of those rules — that the module exports the entrypoint, accepts the host's abi_version, fills the descriptor, and destroys cleanly.
It links no Xmip code. A module written in C, Go or C# is probed exactly the same way, which is the property the boundary exists to have.
One probe serves every surface, and deliberately so: two surfaces answering one question through one boundary is the property ADR-0014 exists to guarantee. The one thing they differ on is where a module's log lines go — the cli writes them to stderr as they arrive, a cmdlet has a verbose stream — so the caller passes a sink and the probe judges nothing about it.

member.name: T:Xmip.Abi.Operate.NativeRuntime
member.summary: The runtime's native library: its file name on this platform, and the one way this binding loads and releases it. and both load through here, and no host loads it any other way.
member.remarks:
The platform is asked here and nowhere else ().
On a desktop or a server a copy is loaded, never the build output itself. A loaded library is locked for as long as this process lives, and the path configured in development is the runtime's own target/debug — so every GUI left running made the next cargo build fail with a locked .dll, and the fix was always "stop the GUI first". Copying costs one file write and removes the hazard for good. The copy is read sharing write and delete, so it never refuses the build writing the library at that moment either: a plain copy shares read only, and a write landing during it failed (a surface's watch reading a library as the next one was written; found 2026-10-12). A library caught half written does not load and says why; the write's end is a change the watch notices, and it is read again.
On a phone there is no file to copy. Android carries the library inside the application package, and it is loaded by its name; iOS links it statically from an xcframework, and its exports are the main program's (ADR-0014, amendment 2026-10-14). build/Xmip.Abi.Native.props puts it there for a host that imports it. A path found by a surface's rule names no library on a phone and is kept only to be shown.

member.summary: The operator boundary as include/xmip_operate.h declares it, crossed by P/Invoke. ADR-0012 clause 1 applies here too: the header is normative and this is not; where they differ, the header is right and this is a defect. One binding for every surface — the cli, the PowerShell module and the GUI all hold one of these, and none of them declares a struct of its own (ADR-0014, amendment of 2026-08-26). What it asks has no node behind it — starting a plan and validating a document; a running node is operated over gRPC at its operate listener (; ADR-0014, amendment 2026-10-13).
